industry.ipm: Indian domestic formulations market ₹2,565 bn in FY26, +9.9% (IQVIA, via Mankind AR FY26 industry section); Abbott India: the IPM 'has historically delivered 8-9% growth', volume growth 'moderate at 5-6%', pricing 'stable and regulated' (AR FY26 MD&A)
industry.ipmGrowth: IPM growth rose to double digits in 2026: Q1FY27 IPM +13.0% ex-tirzepatide (Mankind deck); ~12% IQVIA growth for Abbott India's brands in the June quarter (ICICI Direct)
industry.pricing: Scheduled (NLEM) drugs: ceiling prices +0.65% from 1-Apr-2026 (WPI 2025); non-scheduled: up to 10% a year. ~26% of Abbott's own portfolio is NLEM (Thyronorm fully)
industry.glp1: Semaglutide's patent expired 20-Mar-2026; 20+ companies launched, Novo cut prices up to 48%. Abbott commercialises Extensior (second Ozempic brand) from Feb-2026; Rybelsus (Novo, marketed by Abbott) fell 16% (IQVIA MAT Jul-26)
industry.insulin: Novo Nordisk is winding down cartridge and pen insulin formats in India (Apr-2025); Biocon, Wockhardt, Eris and Lupin are expanding to fill a ~₹450-600 cr gap
industry.mnc: MNC pharma in India (Abbott India, Sanofi India, Pfizer, GSK Pharma) run asset-light models with high payouts, parent-sourced brands and limited new-molecule pipelines; Abbott India is the largest and fastest-growing listed MNC (ICICI Direct: 'standout performer among MNCs')

brokers.thesis: Core portfolio grows with the IPM (+10% MAT Jul-26) but Udiliv, Digene and Duphaston lag and the 35% Novo portfolio declines; growth normalises to 8-9%, so multiple cut from 40x to 32x
Power brands (Thyronorm, Cremaffin Plus, Vertin, Influvac) offset Novo-led fluctuations; Q1 may be an aberration; premium justified by brand stickiness and 75 launches planned in five years

strengths: Category-leading brands with decades of prescriber trust (Thyronorm, Udiliv, Duphalac, Cremaffin, Digene, Vertin, Duphaston)
Access to Abbott's global brands and in-licensing at no royalty
Asset-light model, ~0 capex, 35%+ return on equity, ₹4,400 cr of cash
weaknesses: No own R&D pipeline; launches are line extensions and in-licensed products
35% of revenue is a low-margin distribution business that depends on Novo Nordisk's choices
Key molecules face generics (dydrogesterone) and price control (levothyroxine)

critiques: Growth has slowed to 8% (FY26) and 4% (Q1FY27); the 15-17% EPS growth of FY21-25 came partly from margin expansion that is now mature
BOBCAPS (3-Sep-2026): normalised growth 8-9%, multiple cut to 32x
The Novo portfolio (35% of sales) is shrinking: cartridges discontinued, Mixtard −31%, Rybelsus −16% after semaglutide generics; Extensior faces 20+ generics
Udiliv (+3% MAT Jul-26), Digene (−1%) and Duphaston (+6%) grow below the market; dydrogesterone faces cheaper generics
No earnings calls since 2022; the company does not split own vs partner revenue, so investors rely on IQVIA/Pharmarack
Thyronorm (largest own brand) is fully price-controlled; ~26% of own business is NLEM; the FY27 WPI increase is only 0.65%
Cash (₹4,400 cr, 7.7% of market value) earns ~6% pre-tax and the parent decides how much comes back as dividends
gaps: Abbott India does not disclose revenue by therapy, by brand or own vs partner (Novo) business; we use BOBCAPS' company-sourced split (FY21-24) and its 65/35 estimate for FY26
No management guidance: no earnings calls or presentations since Sep-2022
The economics of the Novo distribution agreement (margin, term, renewal) are not disclosed
NLEM share of the own portfolio is last disclosed for 2022 (26%); no update
Medical representative count last disclosed by a broker for FY24 (~3,250)
Broker notes from houses other than BOBCAPS and ICICI dated by 30-Sep-2026 not found; ICICI Securities institutional's Nov-2025 note read only via a summary; Sharekhan's Sep-2025 method not disclosed
Half-year (Sep-2025) balance sheet treasury not used for the EV history; net cash between year-ends is interpolated
conflicts: BOBCAPS lists 'increase in royalty from the parent company' as a key risk, but the AR FY26 says no price is paid or payable for marketing rights obtained from Abbott affiliates and no royalty line appears in related-party transactions; we follow the annual report
BOBCAPS' FY26 revenue base differs between notes (₹6,929 cr in Aug-2026, ₹6,827 cr in Sep-2026); we use the reported ₹6,929 cr
BOBCAPS shows free float of 50% (2026 notes) and 24% (2025 initiation); the shareholding pattern gives 25.0%

Screener's EV/EBITDA for Abbott includes other income in EBITDA and deducts only cash equivalents (not long-term deposits); we compute our own EV/EBITDA (operating EBITDA, all treasury deducted) for the cross-check
Press summaries give Q1FY27 revenue as ₹1,889 cr (total income incl. other income) and ₹1,814 cr (revenue from operations); we use ₹1,813.7 cr
